summary: A passage from Book 4 (part 121) of a fiction work. Ana strikes a wizard for toying with a desperate girl, Valentine, and warns Valentine to be smart rather than make a tragedy of herself. The wizard tells Ana to see to others and offers Valentine work as a stage-magic-style assistant, promising to look after her family in exchange for a favor due in two days. Valentine agrees to the deal and they shake hands.
one_line: Ana slaps a wizard for mistreating Valentine, then Valentine strikes a deal with him to serve as an assistant in exchange for protection of her family.
key_facts: Ana crosses the room and slaps the wizard hard enough to rock his head back, leaving the print of her open hand on his cheek.
Ana tells the wizard: "Don't you toy with this little girl."
Ana tells Valentine: "Be smart or be gone. I won't watch you make a tragedy of yourself."
Ana says Valentine is old enough to stand her ground and that there are a thousand ways to survive that do not involve lying on your back.
The wizard tells Ana to go and see to the others and says he will negotiate in the best of faith with Valentine.
The wizard brings Valentine a plate of goose-liver dumplings smothered in white gravy.
The wizard eats a big toasted corned beef sandwich that oozes brown mustard.
The wizard describes his offer by comparing himself to a stage magician who has an army of assistants.
Valentine says she is leaving in five days.
The wizard says the favor he has in mind must be performed the day after tomorrow.
The wizard promises: "I always take care of my assistants' families."
Valentine and the wizard shake hands to agree to the deal.

entities.name: Ana
entities.role: blonde woman who slaps the wizard and warns Valentine to be smart; called Anushla by the wizard

entities.name: Valentine
entities.role: young girl who stands her ground before Ana and the wizard and agrees to work for the wizard

entities.name: the wizard
entities.role: magician who tries to recruit Valentine as an assistant and promises to care for her family
